Augmenting the reinforcement learning reward function with physics-based property predictions, such as DFT-calculated electron affinity and GCMC-simulated surface area, will yield a significantly higher percentage of generated covalent triazine framework substrates passing expert material-specific filters for supercapacitor applications than using expert-defined structural filters alone.

Employing multi-objective reinforcement learning to independently optimize symmetry, flatness, conjugation, and cyclization constraints will eliminate the strong negative correlation between internal diversity and expert filter pass rates observed under single-objective scalar rewards for CTF substrate generation.

A multi-objective reinforcement learning strategy enforcing a minimum internal Tanimoto diversity threshold during reward optimization will generate covalent triazine framework substrates with both higher percentages of molecules passing expert-defined filters and greater structural diversity than conventional single-objective reinforcement learning.
